answer: Each identity registers one mesa salt pan, locks a 70-credit bond to its pan key, and at dawn files ocean brine intake, pan area, and salt yield. Auditors recompute yield from intake by the public salt table for that dawn temperature; a shortfall over 5 percent or a reused reading burns the bond. A first pan pays 28 credits; the kth pan by one funder pays 28+6(k-1), so the 1000th costs 6022. For 1000 fakes, fees total 3,025,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-pan ring fails: rented pans carry the lender key and collide in the register. An honest agent pays 28 once, then recovers its bond.
